summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, antiphospholipid syndrome, and a history of chronic pain and seizure disorder was admitted for right vulvar cellulitis following an office incision and drainage of sebaceous cysts that failed outpatient treatment with Bactrim. She was afebrile and hemodynamically stable, with no leukocytosis. Treatment was initiated with vancomycin and Unasyn, later transitioned to vancomycin and levaquin after clarification of a mild penicillin allergy. MRSA screens were negative, supporting de-escalation of therapy. An ultrasound showed no abscess, only cellulitis and a right vulvar cyst, avoiding further intervention. She underwent hemodialysis on hospital days 1 and 3, with improvement in creatinine and potassium. Warfarin was restarted on day 2 after ultrasound confirmed no abscess, with INR rising from 1.0 to 1.1. By day 4, her infection had significantly improved, she was ambulating independently, and was discharged home on oral levaquin and her baseline medications with follow-up instructions.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 5 chronic kidney disease or end stage renal disease
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Surgical operation with transplant of whole organ as the cause of abnormal reaction of the patient, or of later complication, without mention of misadventure at the time of the procedure
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
Personal history of transient ischemic attack (TIA), and cerebral infarction without residual deficits
